recent_posts.title: Using Lumalabs UNI-1 to generate styled infographics for teaching programming concepts
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of using Lumalabs UNI-1, an AI image generation model, to create visually styled infographics for teaching programming concepts like dependency injection in Android with Koin. The model supports multiple visual styles (handcrafted diorama, blueprint, retro risographic, paper cut shadow box) from short prompts, can split infographics for different social media aspect ratios, and also supports image editing tasks like modifying facial expressions. An API is available for building custom apps around the model.

recent_posts.title: AI-Driven APG 9 Migration using Android Skills and Firebender - KMP Project
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of migrating a Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) project to Android Gradle Plugin 9 (AGP9) using AI-powered Android Skills and the Firebender AI tool. The process involves using a pre-built AGP9 migration skill (a structured markdown guide with instructions) fed to the AI to automate the migration steps. Key changes include creating a new Android app module to replace the compose app module, switching from the Android library plugin to the Kotlin Multiplatform library plugin, upgrading Gradle wrapper versions, resolving Firebase dependency issues, and restructuring modules (app-core, app-nav). The AI handles most of the heavy lifting while the developer reviews and accepts changes, with version control providing a safety net.

recent_posts.title: Local Database on the Web - Kotlin Multiplatform Tutorial
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step walkthrough of integrating the Room 3 database library into a Kotlin Multiplatform project targeting both Android and WebAssembly (WASM/JS). Covers project setup, dependencies (SQLite Web, SQLite WASM, SQLite WASM Worker), the Web Worker API requirement for browser-based SQLite operations, the OPFS (Origin Private File System) storage layer, CORS headers configuration, and how to inspect the local database file using the OPFS browser extension and DB Browser for SQLite.

recent_posts.title: Why don't add multiple Paywalls?  Dynamic Onboarding with RevenueCat
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step walkthrough of building a dynamic onboarding flow for Android using RevenueCat. The tutorial covers setting up a RevenueCat project with products, entitlements, and offerings, creating two distinct paywalls (a free trial paywall and a multi-package premium paywall) via the RevenueCat dashboard, and integrating the SDK into a Jetpack Compose Android app. The app presents users with a short questionnaire, calculates a score based on their answers, and dynamically displays the appropriate paywall. Key concepts include initializing the RevenueCat SDK in the Application class, modeling questions and answers with Kotlin data classes, using a ViewModel for state management, and rendering paywalls with the RevenueCat Paywall composable.

recent_posts.title: Google Play Store opens up billing and third-party stores for Android developers
recent_posts.summary: Google is making major changes to the Play Store following the Epic Games vs. Google legal battle. Developers will now be able to use alternative billing systems (like Stripe, Lemon Squeezy, or RevenueCat) alongside or instead of Google Play billing, and can direct users to external websites for purchases. Third-party app stores will also be allowed to host Android apps with fewer security warnings. Fee structure is changing too: developers using Google billing will pay a ~5% billing fee plus a reduced service fee starting at 20% for new installs, with lower rates for high-quality apps. These changes are set to roll out globally by September 30, 2027.

recent_posts.title: Tap to Exit with Navigation 3 - Kotlin Multiplatform (Android/iOS)
recent_posts.summary: A tutorial on implementing a tap-to-exit confirmation dialog using the Navigation 3 library in a Kotlin Multiplatform project targeting Android and iOS. It covers creating an alert dialog with confirm/dismiss buttons, using BackHandler to intercept the system back button only when the back stack has one screen remaining, and calling activity.finish() on confirmation. The iOS side is addressed separately, noting that Apple's Human Interface Guidelines discourage programmatic app termination, so the feature is recommended for Android only.

recent_posts.title: How to migrate your Koin modules to use the new compiler plugin DSL
recent_posts.summary: Koin now supports a Kotlin compiler plugin (version 0.3.0) that eliminates the need for manual get() calls in dependency injection modules. The plugin auto-detects constructor parameters at compile time, works with both DSL and annotations, and generates no visible files. The tutorial walks through migrating existing Koin modules to the new DSL, covering viewModel declarations without double-colon syntax, single bindings using the bind function, multiple interface bindings with bindOf, named qualifiers, and the new injectedParameter annotation. Requires Koin 4.2.0-RC1 and Kotlin 2.3.20-beta1 or newer.

recent_posts.title: Apple authentication with Firebase - Kotlin Multiplatform (CMP) Android/iOS Tutorial
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of implementing Sign in with Apple using Firebase in a Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) project targeting both Android and iOS. Covers setting up the Apple provider in Firebase, enabling the Sign in with Apple capability in Xcode, creating App IDs, Service IDs, and keys in the Apple Developer portal, configuring the KMP-Auth library, and verifying the flow works end-to-end in a simulator.

recent_posts.title: How to create unique App Icon for your next Project
recent_posts.summary: A workflow for creating app icons cheaply using AI tools and Figma. The process involves three steps: using ChatGPT to generate a detailed image prompt based on your app description, feeding that prompt into an AI image generator (imagegpt.io) to produce a PNG icon, and finally importing the result into Figma to manually trace and vectorize it using the pen tool and shapes. The approach costs roughly $10 for 600 AI-generated images and replaces hiring a designer for $200–$500.

recent_posts.title: Swipeable library for Compose Multiplatform adds swipe gestures to any component
recent_posts.summary: Introduction to Swipeable, a new Compose Multiplatform library that adds swipe gestures to any composable component across Android, iOS, and other targets. It supports two modes (reveal and dismiss), customizable background colors (solid or gradient), real-time swipe progress tracking, and predefined animations. Usage involves wrapping a UI component in the Swipeable composable and configuring direction, behavior, threshold, and action callbacks. A to-do app demo illustrates swipe-to-delete and swipe-to-complete interactions.
